title: Fly over Attabad Lake
credits: 3D: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Welcome to Hunza, in Pakistan's far north, high in the Karakoram mountains.
Let's fly up the valley, following the Hunza River.
Ahead lies the village of Attabad.
In January, twenty ten, a huge landslide came down from these slopes, burying homes, and blocking the river completely.
With nowhere to go, the water began to rise behind it.
Over the following months, a new lake filled the valley, drowning fields, villages, and a long stretch of the Karakoram Highway.
Its water, coloured by fine glacial silt, shines a striking turquoise.
It winds for kilometres between mountain walls, that rise thousands of metres on either side.
Further north lies Gulmit, one of the communities whose land was flooded as the lake grew.
From a disaster, a new landscape was born. Today, it is one of Gilgit-Baltistan's most visited sights.
